Since $x\lt 0,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}x & <0 \\ -x & >0 \\ -3x & >0 \\ 1-3x & >1.\end{aligned}
$$

This means that $1-3x$ is positive for all the values of $x$ that we are considering $(x\lt 0).$ So, we can multiply both sides by $1-3x,$ and solve the resulting inequality as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x+5}{1-3x} & <2 \\ (1-3x)\cdot \frac{x+5}{1-3x} & <(1-3x)\cdot 2 \\ x+5 & <2-6x \\ 7x & <-3 \\ x & <-\frac{3}{7}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the inequality will be the numbers that satisfy both $x \lt 0$ and $x \lt -\dfrac{3}{7}.$ So, the solution to our inequality is $x \lt -\dfrac{3}{7}.$

Note that the factor $2{sin}^{2}⁡x-3$ is always negative. We know this because

$$
0\le {sin}^{2}⁡x\le 1\,⇒\,-3\le 2{sin}^{2}⁡x-3\le -1.
$$

Since $2{sin}^{2}⁡x-3$ is always negative, we can multiply both sides of the inequality by this quantity, but we have to remember to flip the sign of the inequality. By doing this, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x+2}{2{sin}^{2}⁡x-3} & >\frac{4-3x}{2{sin}^{2}⁡x-3} \\ (2{sin}^{2}⁡x-3)\cdot \frac{x+2}{2{sin}^{2}⁡x-3} & <(2{sin}^{2}⁡x-3)\cdot \frac{4-3x}{2{sin}^{2}⁡x-3} \\ x+2 & <4-3x \\ 4x & <2 \\ x & <\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
